findings.evidence: ProactiveRefreshScheduler._fireRefresh() never rescheduled after a successful refresh, so proactive refresh fired exactly once per login.
findings.why_it_matters: Every subsequent refresh cycle silently fell back to the reactive 401 path, violating the phase's Design Constraint that proactive refresh be demonstrably time-triggered, not only 401-triggered.
findings.required_action: After a successful onRefreshDue(), call scheduleFromTokenStore() again to re-arm the next proactive cycle.
findings.resolution: _fireRefresh() now calls scheduleFromTokenStore() again immediately after a successful onRefreshDue(); verified by a new two-consecutive-cycle test in proactive_refresh_scheduler_test.dart.

findings.evidence: _newGatewayDio() built BaseOptions with only baseUrl — no connectTimeout/receiveTimeout/sendTimeout anywhere in lib/.
findings.why_it_matters: Every external call (login, logout, refresh, and future call sites through the same Dio instance) could hang indefinitely, stranding AuthBloc in AuthAuthenticating.
findings.required_action: Set connectTimeout/receiveTimeout/sendTimeout on the shared BaseOptions used by _newGatewayDio().
findings.resolution: AppConfig now defines connectTimeout/receiveTimeout/sendTimeout (10s each); _newGatewayDio() wires them into BaseOptions, applied to both ApiClient's and TokenRefresher's Dio instances.

findings.evidence: Login response body fields were force-cast (as String/as int) with no validation, and AuthBloc caught only `on ApiException`.
findings.why_it_matters: A malformed 2xx response threw a raw TypeError that the bloc's catch did not handle, permanently stranding it in AuthAuthenticating with no route to AuthError.
findings.required_action: Validate the response shape at the boundary, or broaden AuthBloc's catch to convert unexpected exceptions into AuthError.
findings.resolution: AuthBloc._onLoginRequested now uses a broad catch (e) and emits AuthError(e is ApiException ? e : UnknownApiException(e.toString())), so any failure reaches a reachable AuthError state.

findings.evidence: Gateway route strings ('/api/iam/auth/login', '/logout', '/refresh') are hardcoded literals split across two files.
findings.why_it_matters: Later phases (2, 6, 7) add more call sites against this same gateway; route strings without a single source will drift as the surface grows.
findings.required_action: Consider a small route-constants holder before more features add their own scattered literals. Not blocking at this phase's size (3 single-use literals).
